title: CBSE Class 9 Mathematics Mock Paper 3 (Exam Simulator / Authentic School Level)
description: Authentic full-length Class 9 CBSE Mathematics examination modeled directly on School Periodic Assessments and CBSE board question patterns.

questions.prompt: The point of intersection of the coordinate axes is called the:
questions.answer: (c) Origin
questions.markingScheme: • Point where x-axis meets y-axis is the Origin (0, 0) [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Coordinates are (0, 0).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an irrational number?
questions.answer: (c) √7
questions.markingScheme: • √4 = 2 (rational); 3√18/√2 = 3√9 = 9 (rational); √9 = 3 (rational); √7 is non-perfect square ⇒ irrational [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Simplify expressions before classifying.

questions.prompt: The coefficient of x<sup>2</sup> in the polynomial 2 - x<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>3</sup> is:
questions.answer: (c) -1
questions.markingScheme: • Term containing x<sup>2</sup> is -x<sup>2</sup> = (-1)x<sup>2</sup> ⇒ coefficient is -1 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Always include the negative sign with the coefficient.

questions.prompt: If the side of an equilateral triangle is 'a', then its height (altitude) is:
questions.answer: (a) (√3 / 2) a
questions.markingScheme: • By Pythagoras theorem in half-triangle: h = √[a<sup>2</sup> - (a/2)<sup>2</sup>] = √(3a<sup>2</sup>/4) = (√3/2)a [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Do not confuse altitude (√3/2)a with area (√3/4)a^2.

questions.prompt: The value of (x - 2)(x + 2)(x<sup>2</sup> + 4) is:
questions.answer: (a) x4 - 16
questions.markingScheme:
• (x - 2)(x + 2) = x2 - 4.
(x2 - 4)(x2 + 4) = (x2)2 - 42 = x4 - 16 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Repeated difference of squares.

questions.prompt: If the area of an equilateral triangle is 16√3 cm<sup>2</sup>, its perimeter is:
questions.answer: (a) 24 cm
questions.markingScheme:
• (√3 / 4) a2 = 16√3 ⇒ a2 = 64 ⇒ a = 8 cm.
Perimeter = 3a = 3(8) = 24 cm [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: First solve for side length a, then multiply by 3.

questions.prompt: The decimal expansion of the number √2 is:
questions.answer: (d) Non-terminating non-recurring
questions.markingScheme: • Every irrational number has a non-terminating non-recurring expansion [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: 1.414 is only an approximation.

questions.prompt: A point both of whose coordinates are negative lies in:
questions.answer: (c) Quadrant III
questions.markingScheme: • Both x < 0 and y < 0 defines Quadrant III [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: (-, -) is Quadrant III.

questions.prompt: If x + y + z = 0, then x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup> + z<sup>3</sup> + 3xyz equals:
questions.answer: (b) 6xyz
questions.markingScheme:
• When x + y + z = 0, x3 + y3 + z3 = 3xyz.
Adding 3xyz gives 3xyz + 3xyz = 6xyz [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Carefully read the question prompt: it asks for x^3 + y^3 + z^3 + 3xyz.

questions.prompt: The zero of the zero polynomial is:
questions.answer: (c) Any real number
questions.markingScheme: • For p(x) = 0, p(c) = 0 for every real number c. Thus every real number is a zero [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Crucial distinction: Degree is not defined, but zero is ANY real number.

questions.prompt: If the perimeter of a triangle is 30 cm and its sides are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3, can such a triangle exist?
options: (c) No, because sum of two sides equals the third side
questions.answer: (c) No, because sum of two sides equals the third side
questions.markingScheme:
• 1x + 2x + 3x = 6x = 30 ⇒ x = 5 cm. Sides are 5, 10, 15.
5 + 10 = 15, violating triangle inequality a + b > c [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Sum of two sides must be strictly GREATER than the third side.

questions.prompt: The value of (125)<sup>-1/3</sup> is:
questions.answer: (b) 1/5
questions.markingScheme: • 125 = 5<sup>3</sup> ⇒ (5<sup>3</sup>)<sup>-1/3</sup> = 5<sup>-1</sup> = 1/5 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Negative power inverts base.

questions.prompt: Abscissa of all points on the y-axis is:
questions.answer: (a) 0
questions.markingScheme: • Any point on y-axis is of the form (0, y), so its abscissa is always 0 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Abscissa is distance from y-axis, which is zero on the y-axis itself.

questions.prompt: If x<sup>2</sup> + kx + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3) for all x, then the value of k is:
questions.answer: (c) 5
questions.markingScheme: • (x + 2)(x + 3) = x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6 ⇒ k = 5 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Coefficient matching.

questions.prompt: The sides of a triangle are 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm. Its area is:
questions.answer: (b) 6 cm2
questions.markingScheme: • 3<sup>2</sup> + 4<sup>2</sup> = 25 = 5<sup>2</sup> ⇒ Area = (1/2) × 3 × 4 = 6 cm<sup>2</sup> [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Standard Pythagorean triangle.

questions.prompt: The degree of the constant polynomial -10 is:
questions.answer: (b) 0
questions.markingScheme: • -10 = -10x<sup>0</sup> ⇒ Degree is 0 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Degree of non-zero constant is 0.

questions.prompt: Which of the following points lies in Quadrant IV?
questions.answer: (b) (5, -3)
questions.markingScheme: • x > 0 and y < 0 is Quadrant IV [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: (+, -) represents Quadrant IV.

questions.prompt: The value of ( √3 + √2 )( √3 - √2 ) is:
questions.answer: (b) 1
questions.markingScheme: • (√3)<sup>2</sup> - (√2)<sup>2</sup> = 3 - 2 = 1 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Difference of squares.

questions.prompt:
Assertion (A): The sum of (2 + √3) and (2 - √3) is a rational number.
Reason (R): The sum of two irrational numbers can sometimes be a rational number.
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.answer: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.markingScheme: • (2 + √3) + (2 - √3) = 4, which is rational. Reason correctly states this property [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Conjugate irrationals cancel radical parts upon addition.

questions.prompt:
Assertion (A): The point (0, 7) lies on the y-axis.
Reason (R): The x-coordinate of every point lying on the y-axis is 0.
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.answer: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.markingScheme: • (0, 7) has x = 0, which directly matches the property in (R) [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Direct definition verification.

questions.prompt: Find the value of (256)<sup>- (4<sup>-3/2</sup>)</sup>.
questions.answer:
1. First simplify the inner exponent 4-3/2:
4-3/2 = (22)-3/2 = 2-3 = 1 / 23 = 1/8.

2. Now substitute into main expression:
(256)- (1/8) = (28)-1/8 = 2-1 = 1/2.
questions.markingScheme:
• Evaluating inner exponent 4-3/2 = 1/8: 1 mark
• Evaluating (256)-1/8 = 1/2: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Work from innermost exponent outwards.

questions.prompt: If x = 1 is a zero of polynomial p(x) = ax<sup>2</sup> - 3(a - 1)x - 1, find the value of a.
questions.answer:
Since x = 1 is a zero, p(1) = 0:
a(1)2 - 3(a - 1)(1) - 1 = 0
a - 3a + 3 - 1 = 0
-2a + 2 = 0 ⇒ 2a = 2 ⇒ a = 1.
questions.markingScheme:
• Setting p(1) = 0: 1 mark
• Solving -2a + 2 = 0 ⇒ a = 1: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Distribute -3 carefully: -3(a - 1) = -3a + 3.

questions.prompt: Find the area of an equilateral triangle whose perimeter is 180 cm.
questions.answer:
Side a = 180 / 3 = 60 cm.
Area = (√3 / 4) a2 = (√3 / 4) × 602 = (√3 / 4) × 3600 = 900√3 cm2 (approx 1558.85 cm2).
questions.markingScheme:
• Finding side a = 60 cm: 0.5 mark
• Applying formula Area = 900√3 cm2: 1.5 marks
questions.examinerTip: Can leave answer as 900√3 cm^2.

questions.prompt: Factorize: 4x<sup>2</sup> + 9y<sup>2</sup> + 16z<sup>2</sup> + 12xy - 24yz - 16xz.
questions.answer:
Write in form A2 + B2 + C2 + 2AB + 2BC + 2CA:
Notice that terms with z (yz and xz) are negative ⇒ z has a negative sign.
= (2x)2 + (3y)2 + (-4z)2 + 2(2x)(3y) + 2(3y)(-4z) + 2(-4z)(2x)
= (2x + 3y - 4z)2 or (2x + 3y - 4z)(2x + 3y - 4z).
questions.markingScheme:
• Identifying negative sign on 4z: 1 mark
• Writing factorized form (2x + 3y - 4z)2: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Examine which variable is common to the negative cross-terms (here z is common to -24yz and -16xz).

questions.prompt: In which quadrant or on which axis do the points lie: A(2, 0), B(-3, 4), C(1, -2), D(0, -5)?
questions.answer:
• A(2, 0): Positive x-axis
• B(-3, 4): Quadrant II
• C(1, -2): Quadrant IV
• D(0, -5): Negative y-axis
questions.markingScheme: • 0.5 mark for each correct answer
questions.examinerTip: Full 2 marks for simple direct classification.

questions.prompt: Show that 0.2353535... = 0.235̅ can be expressed in the form p/q, and state the prime factorization of q.
questions.answer:
Let x = 0.2353535...
10x = 2.353535... --- (1)
1000x = 235.353535... --- (2)
Subtract (1) from (2):
990x = 233 ⇒ x = 233 / 990.

Prime factorization of denominator 990:
990 = 10 × 99 = (2 × 5) × (9 × 11) = 2 × 32 × 5 × 11.
Since it contains prime factors other than 2 and 5 (specifically 3 and 11), the decimal expansion is non-terminating recurring.
questions.markingScheme:
• Deriving x = 233/990: 2 marks
• Prime factorization 990 = 2 × 32 × 5 × 11: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Connecting decimal type to prime factors of denominator.

questions.prompt: Find the zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = (x - 2)<sup>2</sup> - (x + 2)<sup>2</sup>, and verify its degree.
questions.answer:
1. Expand p(x):
p(x) = (x2 - 4x + 4) - (x2 + 4x + 4)
= x2 - 4x + 4 - x2 - 4x - 4
= -8x.

2. Degree of p(x) = -8x is 1 (Linear polynomial).

3. To find zero, set p(x) = 0:
-8x = 0 ⇒ x = 0.
The zero of the polynomial is 0.
questions.markingScheme:
• Correct expansion and simplification to -8x: 1.5 marks
• Stating degree is 1: 0.5 mark
• Solving x = 0: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Direct question from School Exam PA-2 Section C (Question 31).

questions.prompt: If 2x + 3y = 13 and xy = 6, find the value of 8x<sup>3</sup> + 27y<sup>3</sup>.
questions.answer:
Cubing both sides of 2x + 3y = 13:
(2x + 3y)3 = 133
(2x)3 + (3y)3 + 3(2x)(3y)(2x + 3y) = 2197
8x3 + 27y3 + 18xy(2x + 3y) = 2197
Substitute xy = 6 and 2x + 3y = 13:
8x3 + 27y3 + 18(6)(13) = 2197
8x3 + 27y3 + 1404 = 2197
8x3 + 27y3 = 2197 - 1404 = 793.
questions.markingScheme:
• Cubing formula setup: 1 mark
• Substitution of values: 1 mark
• Final evaluation 793: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Direct question from School Exam PA-2 Section C (Question 30).

questions.prompt: The sides of a triangular field are 41 m, 40 m, and 9 m. Find the number of flower beds that can be prepared in the field if each bed occupies an area of 900 cm<sup>2</sup>.
questions.answer:
1. Check for right triangle: 92 + 402 = 81 + 1600 = 1681 = 412.
Area of field = (1/2) × 40 × 9 = 180 m2.

2. Convert field area to cm2:
1 m2 = 10,000 cm2 ⇒ 180 m2 = 180 × 10,000 = 1,800,000 cm2.

3. Area of 1 flower bed = 900 cm2.
Number of beds = 1,800,000 / 900 = 2,000 beds.
questions.markingScheme:
• Area of field = 180 m2: 1.5 marks
• Conversion to 1,800,000 cm2: 0.5 mark
• Number of flower beds = 2,000: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Remember that 1 m^2 = 100 cm × 100 cm = 10,000 cm^2 (not 100 cm^2!).

questions.prompt:
P(3, 2) and Q(7, 7) are two points. Perpendiculars are drawn to the x-axis from P and Q meeting at L and M respectively.
(i) Find the coordinates of L and M.
(ii) Find the length of LM.
(iii) What is the ordinate of the midpoint of segment PQ?
questions.answer:
(i) Coordinates of foot of perpendiculars on x-axis: L(3, 0) and M(7, 0).
(ii) Length of LM = |7 - 3| = 4 units.
(iii) Ordinate of midpoint of PQ = (y1 + y2) / 2 = (2 + 7) / 2 = 9/2 = 4.5 units.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) Coordinates L(3,0) and M(7,0): 1 mark
• (ii) Length LM = 4 units: 1 mark
• (iii) Midpoint ordinate = 4.5: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Direct question from School Exam PA-2 Section C (Question 29).

questions.prompt: If x + y = 12 and xy = 27, find the value of x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup>.
questions.answer:
We know: (x + y)3 = x3 + y3 + 3xy(x + y)
Substitute known values:
123 = x3 + y3 + 3(27)(12)
1728 = x3 + y3 + 81(12)
1728 = x3 + y3 + 972
x3 + y3 = 1728 - 972 = 756.
questions.markingScheme:
• Setup formula: 1 mark
• Calculating 123 = 1728 and 3(27)(12) = 972: 1 mark
• Final answer 756: 1 mark

questions.prompt:
Evaluate without direct cubing using identities:
(i) (0.2)3 - (0.3)3 + (0.1)3 (2.5m)
(ii) (28)3 + (-15)3 + (-13)3 (2.5m)
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) Checking sum = 0 and applying 3abc = -0.018: 2.5 marks
• (ii) Checking sum = 0 and applying 3xyz = 16,380: 2.5 marks
questions.examinerTip: Always verify sum = 0 explicitly in your steps.

questions.prompt: If x = ( √2 + 1 ) / ( √2 - 1 ) and y = ( √2 - 1 ) / ( √2 + 1 ), find the value of x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> - 4xy.
questions.answer:
1. Rationalize x:
x = (√2 + 1)2 / [(√2 - 1)(√2 + 1)] = (2 + 2√2 + 1) / (2 - 1) = 3 + 2√2.

2. Rationalize y:
y = (√2 - 1)2 / [(√2 + 1)(√2 - 1)] = (2 - 2√2 + 1) / (2 - 1) = 3 - 2√2.

3. Compute sums and products:
x + y = (3 + 2√2) + (3 - 2√2) = 6.
xy = (3 + 2√2)(3 - 2√2) = 32 - (2√2)2 = 9 - 8 = 1.

4. Compute x2 + y2:
x2 + y2 = (x + y)2 - 2xy = 62 - 2(1) = 36 - 2 = 34.

5. Compute x2 + y2 - 4xy:
= 34 - 4(1) = 30.
questions.markingScheme:
• Rationalizing x = 3 + 2√2: 1.5 marks
• Rationalizing y = 3 - 2√2: 1.5 marks
• Finding x + y = 6 and xy = 1: 1 mark
• Final evaluation = 30: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Standard CBSE 5-marker board question.

questions.prompt:
A school organized a cleanliness drive in triangular lanes PQ, QR, and RP for Group 1, and PR, RS, and SP for Group 2.
Given: PQ = 7 m, QR = 24 m, RS = 18 m, SP = 13 m, and ∠Q = 90°.
(i) Find the length of diagonal lane PR. (1m)
(ii) Find the area cleaned by Group 1 (ΔPQR). (1m)
(iii) Find the area cleaned by Group 2 (ΔPRS) using Heron's formula. (2.5m)
(iv) Find the total area cleaned by all students. (0.5m)
questions.answer:
(i) In right ΔPQR, PR2 = 72 + 242 = 49 + 576 = 625 ⇒ PR = 25 m.

(ii) Area(ΔPQR) = (1/2) × 7 × 24 = 84 m2.

(iii) In ΔPRS, sides are a = 25 m, b = 18 m, c = 13 m.
Semi-perimeter s = (25 + 18 + 13)/2 = 56/2 = 28 m.
Area(ΔPRS) = √[28(28 - 25)(28 - 18)(28 - 13)]
= √[28 × 3 × 10 × 15]
= √[(4 × 7) × 3 × (2 × 5) × (3 × 5)]
= √[4 × 7 × 32 × 52 × 2] = √[22 × 32 × 52 × 14]
= 2 × 3 × 5 × √14 = 30√14 m2 ≈ 30 × 3.742 = 112.25 m2.

(iv) Total area cleaned = 84 + 30√14 ≈ 84 + 112.25 = 196.25 m2.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) PR = 25 m: 1 mark
• (ii) Area(ΔPQR) = 84 m2: 1 mark
• (iii) Semi-perimeter s = 28 m and Area(ΔPRS) = 30√14 m2 (≈ 112.25 m2): 2.5 marks
• (iv) Total Area = 196.25 m2: 0.5 mark
questions.examinerTip: Direct question from School Exam PA-2 Section D (Question 34).

questions.prompt:
Plot the points P(-2, 2), Q(6, 2), and R(2, 5) on a Cartesian grid.
(i) Find the lengths of the base PQ and the altitude from R to PQ. (2m)
(ii) Find the area of ΔPQR. (1.5m)
(iii) Determine the coordinates of point S such that PQRS forms a parallelogram. (1.5m)
questions.answer:
(i) Segment PQ is horizontal along y = 2.
Length PQ = |6 - (-2)| = 6 + 2 = 8 units.
Point R is at (2, 5). The altitude from R to line y = 2 is the vertical distance = 5 - 2 = 3 units.

(ii) Area(ΔPQR) = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 8 × 3 = 12 sq. units.

(iii) For PQRS to be a parallelogram, opposite sides PQ and SR must be equal and parallel.
PQ is horizontal with length 8 units from x = -2 to x = 6.
Since R is at (2, 5), S must also have y = 5 and be 8 units to the left of R:
x = 2 - 8 = -6.
Therefore, S = (-6, 5).
(Alternatively, midpoint of PR equals midpoint of QS: (-2+2)/2 = 0, so (6+x)/2 = 0 ⇒ x = -6, and y = 5).
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) PQ = 8 units (1 mark), Altitude = 3 units (1 mark): 2 marks
• (ii) Area = 12 sq. units: 1.5 marks
• (iii) S(-6, 5) with geometric justification: 1.5 marks
questions.examinerTip: Coordinate geometry meets parallelogram properties.

questions.prompt:
A residential colony develops a corner public park in the shape of a triangle with boundary lengths 120 m, 160 m, and 200 m.
The ward committee ordered railing around the park at ₹ 15 per meter and turfing the ground at ₹ 10 per m2.

Questions:
(i) Verify whether the triangular park is right-angled. (1m)
(ii) Find the cost of putting railing all around the park. (1m)
(iii) Find the total area of the park using Heron's formula and calculate the cost of turfing. (2m)
questions.answer:
(i) Check Pythagoras theorem: 1202 + 1602 = 14400 + 25600 = 40000 = 2002.
Yes, it is a right-angled triangle (hypotenuse 200 m).

(ii) Perimeter = 120 + 160 + 200 = 480 m.
Cost of railing = 480 × ₹ 15 = ₹ 7,200.

(iii) Semi-perimeter s = 480 / 2 = 240 m.
Area = √[240 × (240 - 120) × (240 - 160) × (240 - 200)]
= √[240 × 120 × 80 × 40] = √[2 × 1202 × 2 × 402] = 120 × 40 × 2 = 9,600 m2.
(Check: (1/2) × 120 × 160 = 9,600 m2).
Cost of turfing = 9,600 × ₹ 10 = ₹ 96,000.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) Verifying 1202 + 1602 = 2002: 1 mark
• (ii) Perimeter = 480 m, Cost = ₹ 7,200: 1 mark
• (iii) Area = 9,600 m2 and Turfing Cost = ₹ 96,000: 2 marks
questions.examinerTip: Direct application of School Exam PA-2 Q36.

questions.prompt:
An architect designs an auditorium ceiling modeled on polynomial expansions:
The cross-sectional acoustic curve is given by A(x) = x3 - 6x2 + 11x - 6.

Questions:
(i) Find the acoustic value A(0) and A(1). (1m)
(ii) Verify whether x = 2 and x = 3 are zeroes of A(x). (2m)
(iii) Express A(x) as a product of three linear factors. (1m)
questions.answer:
(i) A(0) = 0 - 0 + 0 - 6 = -6.
A(1) = 13 - 6(1)2 + 11(1) - 6 = 1 - 6 + 11 - 6 = 0.

(ii) For x = 2: A(2) = 23 - 6(2)2 + 11(2) - 6 = 8 - 24 + 22 - 6 = 0 ⇒ x = 2 is a zero.
For x = 3: A(3) = 33 - 6(3)2 + 11(3) - 6 = 27 - 54 + 33 - 6 = 0 ⇒ x = 3 is a zero.

(iii) Since x = 1, 2, 3 are zeroes, the linear factors are:
A(x) = (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3).
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) A(0) = -6, A(1) = 0: 1 mark
• (ii) Proving A(2) = 0 and A(3) = 0: 2 marks
• (iii) Factorized form (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3): 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Cubic polynomial factorization with 3 distinct zeroes.

questions.prompt:
In a town development project, land plots are laid out on a grid where points denote plot boundary markers: P(0, 0), Q(5, 0), and R(5, 6).

Questions:
(i) What are the lengths of base PQ and vertical boundary QR? (1m)
(ii) Find the area of triangular plot PQR. (1m)
(iii) If a fourth plot marker S is established at (0, 6), prove that PQRS forms a rectangle and find the length of diagonal PR. (2m)
questions.answer:
(i) Length PQ along x-axis = 5 - 0 = 5 units.
Length QR along x = 5 = 6 - 0 = 6 units.

(ii) Since PQ is horizontal and QR is vertical, ∠PQR = 90°.
Area(ΔPQR) = (1/2) × 5 × 6 = 15 sq. units.

(iii) With S(0, 6):
Side PS is along y-axis with length 6 - 0 = 6 units.
Side SR is horizontal along y = 6 with length 5 - 0 = 5 units.
Opposite sides are equal (PQ = SR = 5, QR = PS = 6) and adjacent sides are perpendicular.
Hence, PQRS is a rectangle.
Diagonal PR = √(52 + 62) = √(25 + 36) = √61 units (≈ 7.81 units).
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) PQ = 5, QR = 6: 1 mark
• (ii) Area(ΔPQR) = 15 sq. units: 1 mark
• (iii) Rectangle proof (1 mark) and PR = √61 units (1 mark): 2 marks
questions.examinerTip: Distance formula / Pythagoras theorem on grid.
